history.text: Big Time Wrestling closed, leaving the Mid-Atlantic version as the only United States Championship.
Crockett gained control of the NWA World Heavyweight Championship, and the United States title became secondary.
Ted Turner bought the company and renamed it World Championship Wrestling; the title stayed secondary to the World Championship.
The title was renamed as WCW began pulling away from the NWA.
After WWF bought WCW, the WCW United States Championship was used in WWF programming.
Unified at Survivor Series when Edge beat Test to become Intercontinental Champion.
The title was deactivated following its unification with the Intercontinental Championship.
Reactivated as the WWE United States Championship, a secondary SmackDown title; Eddie Guerrero won the first tournament at Vengeance.
Reactivated as SmackDown!'s secondary title, the counterpart to Raw's Intercontinental Championship.
Champion Matt Hardy was drafted to ECW in the 2008 WWE Draft.
Shelton Benjamin beat Matt Hardy, returning the title to SmackDown.
Champion Montel Vontavious Porter was drafted to Raw in the 2009 WWE Draft.
Champion Sheamus was drafted to SmackDown in the 2011 WWE Draft.
Kofi Kingston beat Sheamus, moving the title back to Raw.
The first brand extension ended, and the title could be defended on both Raw and SmackDown.
The title became officially recognized as a component of the re-established Grand Slam Championship.
The brand extension was reintroduced, and champion Rusev was drafted to Raw.
Champion Kevin Owens moved to SmackDown in the 2017 Superstar Shake-up.
Dolph Ziggler vacated the title, and a tournament was held to crown a new champion, won by Jinder Mahal.
Champion Jinder Mahal was drafted to Raw on night one of the 2018 Superstar Shake-up.
Jeff Hardy beat Mahal and was drafted to SmackDown, returning the title there.
Champion Samoa Joe was drafted to Raw in the 2019 Superstar Shake-up.
Champion Austin Theory was drafted to SmackDown in the 2023 WWE Draft.
